note: WAEC/NECO Physics Paper 1, round 1: full SSCE syllabus - measurements, motion, force and momentum, work/energy/power, machines, pressure and upthrust, heat, waves and sound, light, electricity, electromagnetism and modern physics. Every calculation machine-verified (g = 10 m/s2 where stated).

questions.subject: Physics

questions.explanation: A beam balance compares masses; a spring balance measures weight (a force).

questions.explanation: Averaging the readings: (20.5 + 20.7 + 20.6) ÷ 3 = 20.6 cm.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.explanation: Vectors have both magnitude and direction; velocity is speed in a stated direction.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.explanation: Distance has magnitude only, with no direction attached.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A train travels the first half of a journey at 30 km/h and the second half at 60 km/h. Which statement is true about the journey?
questions.B: The average speed is less than 45 km/h
questions.C: The average speed is more than 45 km/h
questions.D: The average speed cannot be found
questions.explanation: More time is spent on the slower half, so the average is pulled below the simple mean of 45 km/h.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of these is an example of uniform acceleration?
questions.B: A car turning a corner at constant speed
questions.C: A freely falling stone in vacuum
questions.D: A bus moving at constant speed
questions.explanation: A falling body gains equal velocity in equal times; turning at constant speed changes only direction.

questions.explanation: From F = ma, a = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 m/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Newton's third law implies that when a boy kicks a ball,
questions.A: the forces cancel so the ball cannot move
questions.C: the ball exerts an equal and opposite force on his foot
questions.D: only the ball experiences a force
questions.explanation: Forces act in pairs on different bodies: foot on ball and ball on foot.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The friction between a car's tyres and the road is useful because it
questions.D: allows the car to start, stop and turn
questions.explanation: Without friction the wheels would spin and braking would fail.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body in equilibrium under three forces must have the forces
questions.explanation: Balanced forces give zero resultant, so no acceleration occurs.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which statement about mass and weight is correct?
questions.A: Both are exactly the same quantity
questions.B: Weight is constant while mass varies
questions.C: Mass is constant while weight varies with gravity
questions.explanation: Mass is the quantity of matter; weight is the gravitational force on it.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A resultant force of zero acts on a moving body. The body will
questions.B: slow down steadily and then stop
questions.C: come to rest immediately after braking
questions.D: continue moving with the same velocity
questions.explanation: Newton's first law: with no net force the motion stays unchanged.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Why does a passenger lurch forward when a bus brakes suddenly?
questions.A: the seat behind pushes him forward hard
questions.B: his body tends to continue in its state of motion
questions.C: the force of gravity acts forward on him
questions.D: the bus engine pulls his body forward
questions.explanation: Inertia keeps the passenger moving until the seat belt restrains him.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The work done by a force is zero when the force acts
questions.C: perpendicular to the direction of motion
questions.explanation: No component of the force along the motion means no work is done.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: One horsepower is equal to about
questions.explanation: One horsepower is the imperial unit of power, equal to about 746 watts.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A pump lifts 60 kg of water through a height of 5 m every minute. Taking g = 10 m/s², its power is
questions.explanation: Each minute it does 3,000 J of work, so the power is 3,000 ÷ 60 = 50 W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball is thrown upwards. At the highest point of its flight,
questions.A: kinetic energy reaches its greatest value
questions.B: both forms of energy have become zero
questions.C: kinetic energy is zero and potential energy is greatest
questions.D: potential energy falls back down to zero
questions.explanation: The ball momentarily stops, so all its energy is stored as potential energy.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.explanation: MA = load ÷ effort = 200 ÷ 50 = 4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A machine has MA 4 and VR 5. Its efficiency is
questions.explanation: Efficiency = (MA ÷ VR) × 100 = 80%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The efficiency of a real machine is always less than 100% because of
questions.explanation: Work is wasted against friction and lifting moving parts.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a pulley system with four ropes supporting the load, the velocity ratio is
questions.explanation: Each supporting rope shares the load, giving VR equal to the number of ropes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A machine that is a distance multiplier has a velocity ratio that is
questions.explanation: Speed multipliers like bicycles trade force for distance: VR < 1 means effort moves less.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An inclined plane 5 m long raises a load 1 m high. Its velocity ratio is
questions.explanation: VR = length of slope ÷ height = 5 ÷ 1 = 5.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which machine is used to raise water from a well in many Nigerian villages?
questions.A: a hydraulic press for lifting loads
questions.B: a pulley system mounted on a simple frame
questions.C: a system of gears and chains
questions.D: a bicycle wheel and axle system
questions.explanation: A single fixed pulley changes the direction of the effort for easy pulling.

questions.A: absorb the pull of gravity somehow
questions.B: reduce the weight of the person walking
questions.C: increase the pressure under the foot

questions.explanation: The same force over a bigger area gives a smaller pressure.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Heat is transferred through a metal spoon in hot soup mainly by

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Land and sea breezes are caused by
questions.explanation: Air warmed by the land or sea rises and circulates as convection currents.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The vacuum between the walls of a thermos flask reduces heat transfer by
questions.explanation: A vacuum has no particles, so neither conduction nor convection can cross it.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.explanation: Infrared radiation travels through empty space needs no medium.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Evaporation of water in a clay pot keeps the water cool because
questions.A: the water absorbs extra heat from the warm air
questions.B: clay conducts the heat away very quickly indeed
questions.C: the fastest molecules escape and lower the average energy
questions.D: the clay surface reflects the sunlight away
questions.explanation: Only energetic molecules escape, so those left behind are cooler.

questions.explanation: They are parts of one electromagnetic family needing no medium.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A boy claps and hears the echo from a cliff 2 s later. If sound travels at 340 m/s, the cliff is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The pitch of a note depends on its
questions.explanation: Higher frequency is heard as a higher pitch.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The loudness of a sound depends mainly on its
questions.explanation: A bigger amplitude carries more energy and sounds louder.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The bell-in-a-vacuum-jar experiment shows that sound

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which property of light waves shows they are transverse?
questions.explanation: Only transverse waves can be polarised; longitudinal waves cannot.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The image formed by a plane mirror is always
questions.A: real, inverted and laterally inverted always
questions.B: virtual, upright, same size and laterally inverted
questions.C: real, upright and smaller than the object
questions.D: virtual, inverted and the same size as the object
questions.explanation: Plane mirror images are behind the mirror, same size, and reversed left to right.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A girl stands 2 m in front of a plane mirror. The distance between her and her image is
questions.explanation: The image lies 2 m behind the mirror, giving 2 + 2 = 4 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ray strikes a plane mirror at 35° to the normal. The angle of reflection is
questions.explanation: The law of reflection: angle of incidence equals angle of reflection.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A pencil partly dipped in water appears bent because light
questions.B: is refracted at the water surface
questions.explanation: The speed change on entering water bends the rays, displacing the image.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.subject: Physics

questions.explanation: Dispersion separates the colours because each bends by a different amount.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the dispersion of white light by a prism, the colour deviated least is
questions.explanation: Red light has the longest wavelength and is refracted least.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A concave mirror is used in a car headlamp because it
questions.A: forms only virtual images for all positions
questions.B: reflects light from its focus into a parallel beam
questions.C: spreads the incoming light in every direction
questions.D: absorbs the light that strikes its surface
questions.explanation: A bulb at the principal focus reflects off the concave mirror as a parallel beam.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = 1/15 − 1/20 = 1/60, so v = 60 cm in front of the mirror.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A long-sighted person sees distant objects clearly but not near ones. The defect is corrected with a
questions.explanation: The eyeball is too short, so a converging lens brings near rays to a focus on the retina.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The image in a pinhole camera is
questions.explanation: Rays crossing at the pinhole project a real, inverted image on the screen.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a glass rod is rubbed with silk, the rod becomes
questions.explanation: Glass loses electrons to silk, leaving it with a positive charge.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two like charges brought close together will
questions.explanation: Like charges repel; unlike charges attract.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The gold-leaf electroscope is used to
questions.A: measure the resistance of a wire segment
questions.B: measure the size of an electric current
questions.C: detect the presence and sign of electric charge
questions.D: store large amounts of charge for later use
questions.explanation: Charge shared with the leaves makes them diverge, showing charge is present.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A lightning conductor protects a building by
questions.A: reflecting the lightning back into the sky
questions.B: stopping the thunder that follows lightning
questions.C: insulating the roof of the whole building
questions.D: giving charge a safe path down into the earth
questions.explanation: Its pointed tip and thick earth wire channel the discharge harmlessly to ground.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A charge of 12 C flows through a wire in 4 s. The current is
questions.explanation: Current is the rate of flow of charge: I = 12 ÷ 4 = 3 A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A potential difference of 6 V drives a current through a 2 Ω resistor. The current is
questions.explanation: Ohm's law: I = V/R = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two 6 Ω resistors connected in parallel have a total resistance of

questions.q: A 3 Ω resistor and a 6 Ω resistor are connected in parallel. The combined resistance is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A voltmeter is connected in a circuit in
questions.explanation: Its high resistance lets it measure the p.d. across a component without diverting current.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A torch lamp draws 0.5 A from a 4 V supply. The power of the lamp is
questions.explanation: Electrical power is voltage times current: 4 × 0.5 = 2 W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A current of 2 A flows through a 5 Ω resistor. The power dissipated is
questions.explanation: Using P = I²R with I = 2 A gives 4 × 5 = 20 W of heat.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 2 kW heater runs for 3 hours. The energy consumed is
questions.explanation: Energy = power × time = 2 × 3 = 6 kWh.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A family uses 6 kWh of electricity at ₦40 per kWh. The bill is
questions.explanation: Six units at ₦40 each cost 6 × 40 = ₦240.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A fuse rated 5 A in a circuit will blow when the current
questions.explanation: The fuse wire melts above its rating, protecting the appliance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Electrical appliances are earthed so that
questions.A: any leakage current flows safely to the ground
questions.B: they draw a much smaller current overall
questions.C: their working parts last a lot longer
questions.D: they can work without a live wire fitted
questions.explanation: The earth wire gives fault current an easy path, preventing shocks.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The resistance of a wire increases when its
questions.A: length increases or cross-sectional area decreases
questions.B: length decreases and area stays constant
questions.C: cross-sectional area of the wire increases
questions.D: temperature of the conductor falls a little
questions.explanation: R = ρL/A: longer and thinner conductors resist more.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which material allows electric current to pass through it easily?
questions.explanation: Copper is a good conductor with free electrons.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two north poles brought close together will
questions.explanation: Like magnetic poles repel one another.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Outside a bar magnet, the magnetic field lines run from
questions.A: the north pole to the south pole
questions.B: the south pole to the north pole
questions.explanation: By convention field lines leave the north-seeking pole and enter the south pole.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The only metals attracted strongly by magnets are
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic materials are strongly attracted by magnets.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The strength of an electromagnet is increased by
questions.A: increasing the current and the number of turns
questions.B: replacing the iron core with a plastic one
questions.C: reversing the terminals of the battery
questions.D: replacing the coil with a much thinner wire
questions.explanation: More turns, more current and a soft iron core all strengthen the electromagnet.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A compass needle comes to rest pointing
questions.explanation: The magnetised needle aligns itself with the earth's field, roughly north-south.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field experiences a force. This is the principle of the
questions.explanation: The motor effect converts electrical energy to mechanical rotation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A generator produces electricity by
questions.A: rotating a coil in a magnetic field
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic induction: a changing flux through the coil induces an EMF.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A transformer has 1,200 primary turns and 480 secondary turns. If the primary voltage is 240 V, the secondary voltage is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A step-up transformer has more turns on the
questions.A: secondary coil than the primary coil
questions.explanation: More secondary turns raise the voltage delivered.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction states that the induced EMF depends on the
questions.A: rate of change of magnetic flux
questions.explanation: Faster flux changes induce larger EMFs.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the domestic mains supply, the alternating current
questions.A: reverses its direction many times each second
questions.B: flows in only one direction at all times
questions.C: has no measurable voltage at any instant
questions.D: cannot be measured by any instrument
questions.explanation: Nigerian mains AC reverses 50 times each second (50 Hz).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An alpha particle is identical with
questions.explanation: Alpha particles carry two protons and two neutrons, with charge +2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A beta particle is a fast-moving
questions.explanation: Beta decay emits electrons created when a neutron changes into a proton.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which radiation has the greatest penetrating power?
questions.explanation: Gamma rays, being uncharged electromagnetic waves, pass through several cm of lead.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A radioactive isotope has a half-life of 8 days. Starting with 16 g, the mass remaining after 32 days is
questions.explanation: 32 days is four half-lives, so 16 → 8 → 4 → 2 → 1 g.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Uranium-238 emits an alpha particle. The mass number of the daughter nucleus is
questions.explanation: Alpha emission removes 4 from the mass number: 238 − 4 = 234.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The photoelectric effect shows that light behaves as
questions.A: packets of energy carried by particle-like photons
questions.B: continuous waves with no energy packets
questions.C: a magnetic field around a moving charge
questions.D: a kind of sound wave of very high pitch
questions.explanation: Electrons are ejected only above a threshold frequency, one packet per photon.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the photoelectric effect, increasing the intensity of the light increases the
questions.A: number of electrons emitted per second
questions.explanation: More photons per second free more electrons; each electron's energy depends on frequency.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: X-rays are produced when
questions.A: fast electrons strike a metal target
questions.explanation: Sudden deceleration of electrons at the target converts kinetic energy into X-rays.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which is a medical use of X-rays?
questions.explanation: X-rays pass through flesh but are absorbed by bone, imaging fractures.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Nuclear fusion, the source of the sun's energy, is the
questions.A: joining of light nuclei into a heavier one
questions.explanation: Hydrogen nuclei fuse into helium, releasing enormous energy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The half-life of a radioactive element is the time taken for
questions.A: half the atoms present to decay
questions.explanation: Each half-life halves whatever amount remains, whatever the starting mass.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Thick lead shielding is used around radioactive sources because lead
questions.explanation: Lead's dense atoms absorb alpha, beta and much gamma radiation.
